title: Finite-type extraordinary pullback of prime-power pinnings
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $f:T\to S$ be a separated finite-type morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Assume $f$ has a compactification, an open immersion followed by a proper morphism [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $\delta_S$ be a dimension function and let $K$ be a pinned potential dualizing complex for $(S,\delta_S,\Lambda)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Write $f^!$ for the bounded-below exceptional right adjoint of ordinary etale compact support $Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $\delta_T(t)=\delta_S(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$ is a dimension function and $f^!K$ has natural pinnings making it potential for $\delta_T$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. For composable such maps $T\xrightarrow fS\xrightarrow gB$ the right-adjoint transitivity isomorphism $f^!g^!\cong(gf)^!$ preserves these pinnings.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.1.2 and Remark 4.1.3, with coefficient integer ell^n

proof.text: Excellence makes $S$ locally Noetherian and universally catenary, by the definition of excellence. Apply [lem-per-finite-type-dimension-function] to $f$ and $\delta_S$. This gives precisely the asserted dimension function $\delta_T$. Its values are integers since a residue extension for a finite-type map has finite transcendence degree.

For $t\in T$, put $s=f(t)$, $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$ and write $p_s:C_sK\to\Lambda(\delta_S(s))[2\delta_S(s)]$ for the given pinning. Use the actual costalk comparison of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] to define
$$p^f_t=\bigl(a_t^*p_s\bigr)(r)[2r]\circ\beta_{f,t,K}^{-1}:C_t(f^!K)\longrightarrow\Lambda(\delta_T(t))[2\delta_T(t)].$$
Here inverse image of roots of unity identifies $a_t^*\Lambda(m)$ with $\Lambda(m)$, as part of the twist-compatible comparison. The formula is an isomorphism, is natural in pinning-preserving maps of $K$, and is independent of choices, because $\beta$ has these properties. Thus the actual object $f^!K$ has specified pointwise pinnings; potentiality remains to be checked.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1: construction on regular opens in point closures

proof.text: First consider a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ and a potential complex $L$ on $V$. The closed-immersion clause of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] identifies $C_z(i^!L)$ with $C_{i(z)}L$, so the pinning of $i^!L$ is the pinning of $L$. For a geometric point of $Z$, [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient-core] identifies its strict-local ring with the quotient of the strict-local ring of $V$ by the defining ideal. Thus $Z$ remains closed in that strict localization. For an immediate geometric specialization in $Z$, its reduced closure there is therefore also its reduced closure in $V$. Write that closure as $W$ and its inclusions as $W\xrightarrow bZ\xrightarrow iV$. In the defining residue construction, the complex on $W$ for $i^!L$ is $b^!i^!L=(ib)^!L$, exactly the complex on $W$ for $L$. The normalization of $W$, its purely inseparable degree, and its trait transition are identical. Hence the two specialization maps are identical under the costalk identifications. The potentiality equation for $L$ is therefore the potentiality equation for $i^!L$.

source.place: XVII, Definition 1.4.1 and Definition 2.1.2; closed-immersion case of Section 4.4

proof.text: Next let $p:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$ be an affine-space projection with $V$ Noetherian excellent. Its source is Noetherian excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] applied to polynomial coordinate rings. The projection is smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. It is also regular in the sense of [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings]: over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ the ring $R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ is a free, hence flat, $R$-module, and localizations preserve flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism]; for a point $v$ and any field $F\supseteq\kappa(v)$ the base-changed fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}F[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, which is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]. For a potential $L$ on $V$, [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings] gives potential pinnings on $p^*L$ for $\delta_V(p(y))-\dim\mathcal O_{(\mathbf A^d_V)_{p(y)},y}$. Tensoring by the invertible Tate line $(d)$ and shifting by $2d$ carries the defining residue equation to the same equation with every value of the dimension function increased by $d$: on a strict henselian trait the Tate line is constant, and the supported trait model is linear, so its differentials and residue map commute with these operations. Thus $p^*L(d)[2d]$ is potential for that increased function. The smooth-purity isomorphism and its costalk compatibility in [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] identify this pinned object with $p^!L$ carrying exactly the pinnings of Step 2. The same compatibility identifies the increased function with $\delta_V(p(y))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(p(y))}\kappa(y)$. The smooth isomorphism used here is the ordinary-etale, arbitrary-input, excellent-Noetherian one of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change].

source.place: XVII, Section 4.4, final paragraph and smooth-pinning comparison following Lemma 4.4.1

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ about $f(t)$ and a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ about $t$ of the finite-type affine cover of $f^{-1}(V)$ in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra. Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$; the surjection $A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$, $x_j\mapsto b_j$, factors $f|_U$ as a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ followed by its projection $p$. Step 4 makes $p^!(K|_V)$ potential, and Step 3 makes $i^!p^!(K|_V)$ potential. Right-adjoint transitivity identifies this with $(f|_U)^!(K|_V)$. Source locality [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and target open restriction [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint] identify the latter with $(f^!K)|_U$. These ambient adjoint comparisons restrict to the bounded-below objects here: $p^!$ is the displayed twist-shift of $p^*$ and $i^!$ is right-derived supported restriction; their Hom adjunctions on $D^+$ identify them with the stated bounded-below adjoints. The restriction and composition clauses of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] show that its pinnings are the restrictions of the globally defined $p^f_t$, rather than different pinnings on an isomorphic complex. Every immediate specialization can be checked on an open containing its special point, which also contains its general point; its strict-local closure and residue model are unchanged there. Consequently the global pinnings satisfy potentiality. This proves the main assertion.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 4.1.2, final paragraph: affine factorization

proof.text:
For $T\xrightarrow fS\xrightarrow gB$ and $t\mapsto s\mapsto b$, the tower formula [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(t)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(s)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t).$$
Thus the iterated and direct dimension functions agree. Expand the two iterated pinnings using the formula in Step 2. Their inverse comparison is the composite of $\beta_{g,s,K}$ and $\beta_{f,t,g^!K}$, followed by the pullback of the pinning at $b$, with the displayed twist-shifts added. The composition clause of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] identifies that composite with $\beta_{gf,t,K}$. Hence it gives exactly $p^{gf}_t$ under $f^!g^!\cong(gf)^!$. This holds for every $t$, so transitivity preserves the pinnings. When the source is empty all pointwise conditions are vacuous; for an identity map, $r=0$ and the formula returns the original pinning.
